base_member_text: For sides with n=0 (south/east/north here) Nsm_side=(0-1)*iscale+1=-1 (L57-60), so the header writes -1-0-1+1=-1 points for those sides (L261-267); whether FUNWAVE's COUPLING reader tolerates negative counts is external to this file.
audit_member_text: Inactive-side header defect: nsouth, neast, and nnorth are zero on lines 36-38, but the formulas on lines 58-60 yield Nsm=-1. Lines 261, 265, and 267 still write boundary counts derived from those values, producing -1 points for inactive east/south/north sides instead of a nonnegative zero count.

base_member_text: tmp=(III-II)/iscale (L189, repeated L204, L219, L234) is integer/integer division assigned to a real: tmp is 0 for all III<II+iscale and 1 only at III=II+iscale, so the intended linear interpolation degenerates to piecewise-constant (nearest-coarse-point) refinement -- likely bug.
audit_member_text: Definite interpolation defect: I, II, III, and iscale are implicitly INTEGER, so tmp=(III-II)/iscale on the west/east/south/north interpolation paths (west block around line 189 and lines 204, 219, 234) performs integer division before assignment to real tmp. With iscale=2, the interior weight is 0 instead of 0.5, collapsing intended linear interpolation to repeated endpoints.

base_member_text: Ndata is overwritten by each side's read loop (L90, L118, L147, L174) -- the last active side's record count wins; sides with different lengths would silently truncate/extend.

The refinement loop covers III=II..II+iscale inclusive (L188), writing the shared endpoint twice for consecutive I; icount-based sta_NNNN numbering assumes the station file order east->west->south->north matches how mk_station.m generated them ('order should be east, west, south, north' L68 vs the grid_A script's west+south legs).
nsta (L34) is unused; implicit typing throughout (no IMPLICIT NONE); FORMAT 100 (L319) unused.

audit_member_text: Cross-file length/time mismatch: every station read overwrites the shared time vector and scalar Ndata (for example east lines 84-90 and west lines 112-118). The later global loop DO K=1,Ndata at line 183 therefore uses only the last-read station's length and time base for every side and station; if files differ, earlier shorter arrays are read uninitialized or earlier longer samples are silently truncated, and differing timestamps are never compared.
dispositions.rationale: unmatched audit finding (mat=HIGH) | span-reviewed 2026-08-27 not-promoted: nesting stations share one parent time-base by design → shared time/Ndata overwrite benign; MED fragility only if station files differ.

audit_member_text: Out-of-bounds search: lines 251-254 increment Kstart while TIME(Kstart)<time_cut without checking Kstart<=Ndata (or Ntotal). If time_cut exceeds the final available timestamp, TIME is indexed beyond valid data and potentially beyond its allocation before the loop can terminate.
dispositions.rationale: span-verified 2026-08-27: unbounded DO WHILE search over TIME() with no Kstart<=Ndata/Ntotal bound; time_cut past last timestamp reads uninitialized elements and past Ntotal=10000 exceeds allocation (OOB). base missed.

audit_member_text: No configuration checks enforce 0<=nside<=nsta_tot, iscale>0, Nsm_side<=Nb, or valid start/trim bounds before interpolation and implied-DO output indexing; changed inputs can divide by zero or exceed coupling-array bounds.

Station OPEN/READ operations have no IOSTAT/ERR handling other than END= labels. Missing files or malformed records are unchecked fatal errors, and a file containing exactly Ntotal records leaves no capacity to detect additional data.

The configured nsta value on line 34 is not used to validate that nwest+nsouth+neast+nnorth equals the intended number of sequential sta_NNNN files, so filename-to-side mapping can silently drift when side counts are edited.
